subject: 리딩파워 유형편 완성
title: 동물 비계와 내장을 선호했던 초기 인류
fullPassage: Some researchers assumed that early human beings ate mainly the muscle flesh of animals, as we do today. By "meat," they meant the muscle of the animal. Yet focusing on the muscle appears to be a relatively recent phenomenon. In every history on the subject, the evidence suggests that early human populations preferred the fat and organ meat of the animal over its muscle meat. Vilhjalmur Stefansson, an arctic explorer, found that the Inuit were careful to save fatty meat and organs for human consumption while giving muscle meat to the dogs. In this way, humans ate as other large, meat-eating mammals eat. Lions and tigers, for instance, first eat the blood, hearts, livers, and brains of the animals they kill, often leaving the muscle meat for eagles. These organs tend to be much higher in fat.
